newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: French minister urges foreign force for Zaire.
newsitem.headline: French minister urges foreign force for Zaire.

text.p: France's state secretary for humanitarian action Xavier Emanuelli called on Wednesday for a multinational force to be sent to eastern Zaire if rebels fighting to oust the Kinshasa government refused to agree to a ceasefire.

He told the United Nations Human Rights Commission, which this week started its six-week annual session, that the outside world must intervene to protect Rwandan Hutu refugees fleeing the advance of the insurgents, as well as Zairean civilians.
"It is urgent, even vital, to protect these lost people and to provide security for the delivery of aid," declared Emanuelli, who recently visited the region.

"If the ceasefire demanded by the (U.N.) Security Council is not immediately respected, only the despatch of a multinational force can guarantee this essential security and put an end to this hellish flight which has already cost the lives of thousands of people," he said.

He was speaking after the Foreign Ministry in Paris said France would ask its European union partners to help it organise an airlift of humanitarian aid supplies to the city of Kisangani, now under threat of a rebel assault.
Rebel leader Laurent Kabila, who has made clear his movement's aim is the overthrow of President Mobutu Sese Seko, has rejected the ceasefire call.
On Tuesday, a coalition of Zairean exile groups in Switzerland accused France of pushing for intervention to try to save Mobutu, whom Paris has traditionally supported.
Earlier on Wednesday the Justice Minister of Rwanda, Faustin Nteziryayo, told a Geneva news conference he believed France had "ulterior motives" in trying to get an outside force into eastern Zaire.
